```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE,
                      cache = FALSE, fig.align = "center")
```

# Purpose

Auto-ARIMA, ETS, and Theta need a regular daily series, so the thesis inserts a
**zero** on closed days. But a closed store is not a zero-sales day. The zeros
drag a store's estimated level and weekly seasonal down, which can bias the
open-day forecasts low and inflate these models' RMSE, putting them at an unfair
disadvantage.

This file re-runs the three statistical benchmarks on the **same stores and the
same open-day test set**, under two closed-day treatments:

- **zero**: closed days entered as zero sales (the current thesis approach);
- **interp**: closed days treated as missing and filled with
  `forecast::na.interp`, which preserves the level and weekly pattern.

If `interp` lowers the RMSE meaningfully, the statistical benchmarks are stronger
than the thesis reports, and the better numbers should replace the current ones.
Only ARIMA/ETS/Theta are affected; the regression and tree models use the
open-day feature matrix and never see a zero-filled day.

# 1. Packages and configuration

```{r packages}
library(tidyverse); library(lubridate); library(forecast)
TRAIN_CSV <- "train.csv"; STORE_CSV <- "store.csv"
TEST_DAYS <- 42; SEED <- 42; FREQ <- 7
# Quick check on a sample first; set SAMPLE_N <- NULL to run all 1115 (slow).
SAMPLE_N <- 400
set.seed(SEED)
```

# 2. Data

```{r load}
train_raw <- read_csv(TRAIN_CSV, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(Date = as.Date(Date)) %>% arrange(Store, Date)
stores <- sort(unique(train_raw$Store))
if (!is.null(SAMPLE_N)) stores <- sort(sample(stores, SAMPLE_N))
cat("Stores evaluated:", length(stores), "\n")
```

# 3. Per-store evaluation under both treatments

```{r eval}
# For one store: build the daily series, fit each model under each treatment,
# forecast the 42-day horizon, and return squared errors on the OPEN test days.
eval_store <- function(s) {
  d <- train_raw %>% filter(Store == s) %>% arrange(Date)
  n <- nrow(d); if (n <= TEST_DAYS + 2 * FREQ) return(NULL)
  cut <- n - TEST_DAYS
  tr <- 1:cut; te <- (cut + 1):n

  # open test rows are the only ones evaluated (Open == 1 and Sales > 0)
  open_te <- te[d$Open[te] == 1 & d$Sales[te] > 0]
  if (length(open_te) == 0) return(NULL)
  actual  <- d$Sales[open_te]
  pos_h   <- open_te - cut                       # position within the 42-day horizon

  sales0  <- d$Sales[tr]                          # zeros on closed days (raw)
  salesNA <- ifelse(d$Open[tr] == 0 | d$Sales[tr] == 0, NA, d$Sales[tr])

  series <- list(
    zero   = ts(sales0, frequency = FREQ),
    interp = na.interp(ts(salesNA, frequency = FREQ))
  )

  out <- list()
  for (h in names(series)) {
    y <- series[[h]]
    fcs <- list(
      ARIMA = tryCatch(as.numeric(forecast(auto.arima(y, stepwise = TRUE,
                         approximation = TRUE), h = TEST_DAYS)$mean),
                       error = function(e) rep(mean(y), TEST_DAYS)),
      ETS   = tryCatch(as.numeric(forecast(ets(y), h = TEST_DAYS)$mean),
                       error = function(e) rep(mean(y), TEST_DAYS)),
      Theta = tryCatch(as.numeric(thetaf(y, h = TEST_DAYS)$mean),
                       error = function(e) rep(mean(y), TEST_DAYS))
    )
    for (m in names(fcs)) {
      pred <- fcs[[m]][pos_h]
      out[[paste(h, m)]] <- (actual - pred)^2
    }
  }
  imap_dfr(out, ~ tibble(key = .y, sq = .x))
}

res <- map_dfr(stores, eval_store)
```

# 4. Pooled RMSE: zero vs interp

```{r summary}
summ <- res %>%
  separate(key, into = c("Treatment", "Model"), sep = " ") %>%
  group_by(Model, Treatment) %>%
  summarise(RMSE = sqrt(mean(sq)), obs = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  select(-obs) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = Treatment, values_from = RMSE) %>%
  mutate(zero = round(zero), interp = round(interp),
         improvement_pct = round((zero - interp) / zero * 100, 1))
summ
```

# 5. Read-off

```{r verdict}
cat("If `interp` is clearly below `zero`, the zero-fill was inflating the\n",
    "statistical-model RMSE; rerun with SAMPLE_N <- NULL for the full-sample\n",
    "numbers and replace Auto-ARIMA/ETS/Theta in the Stage 1 table.\n")
```
